texts.preamble: A.Srinivas vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 11 November, 2022 Bench: A.Abhishek Reddy, Juvvadi Sridevi The Hon'Ble Sri Justice A.Abhishek Reddy And The Hon'Ble Smt Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Writ Petition No.37038 of 2022 Order:
texts.facts: , the respondent No.2 has passed the impugned detention order dated 03.09.2022. Thereafter, the impugned detention order was passed invoking the draconian preventive detention law and the detenu was sent to jail. The said crimes relied on by the detaining authority do not add up to "disturbing the public order" and they are confined within the ambit and scope of the words "law and order". Since the AAR, J & JS,J offences alleged are under the Prohibition Act, the detenu can certainly be tried and convicted under the said special laws. Therefore, there was no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention law against the detenu. Hence, the impugned orders are legally unsustainable and ultimately, prayed to allow the Writ Petition, as A.Srinivas vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 11 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17740370/ 1 prayed for. 4. The series of crimes allegedly committed by the detenu were sufficient to cause a feeling of insecurity in the minds of the people at large. Therefore, the detaining authority and the Government are justified in passing the impugned AAR, J & JS,J orders. The impugned orders are legally sustainable and ultimately, prayed to dismiss the Writ Petition.
texts.arguments: On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents supported the impugned orders and submitted that the detenu is a 'bootlegger'. He is repeatedly indulging in clandestine business of possession, manufacture and sale of Illicitly Distilled Liquor, in contravention of the provisions of the Prohibition Act, thus, indulging in lawless activities prejudicial to the maintenance of public order, as I.D. liquor is dangerous to the life of general public. The acts of the detenu are prejudicial to the maintenance of public order. The three crimes relied on by the detaining authority amount to disturbance of public order at large. 7. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has, in fact, deprecated the invoking of the preventive law in order to tackle a law and order problem. It was observed that every breach of public peace and every violation of law may create a 'law and order' problem, but does not necessarily create a problem of 'public order'. 8. In Kanu Biswas v. State of West Bengal2, the Hon'ble Apex Court, while discussing the meaning of word 'public order,' held that the question whether a man has only committed a breach of 'law and order' or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the 'public order', is a question of A.Srinivas vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 11 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17740370/ 2 degree and extent of the reach of the act upon the Society. 9. In another recent judgment in Shaik Nazneen v. The State of Telangana and others3, the Hon'ble Apex Court, while referring to its AIR 1966 SC 740 (1972) 3 SCC 831 Judgment dated 22.06.2022 passed in Crl.A.No.908 of 2022 by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. AAR, J & JS,J earlier decisions in Mallada K Sri Ram v. State of Telangana4 and Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana5, held as follows: "15. ... The powers to be exercised under the Preventive Detention Law are exceptional powers which have been given to the Government for its exercise in an exceptional situation as it strikes hard on the freedom and liberty of an individual, and thus cannot be exercised in a routine manner. The distinction between law and order situation and a public order situation has been dealt with by the Supreme Court in a catena of decisions. 16. xxx 17.
